8.4 — Boss Attacks: Patterns & Phases

The boss can be hurt (8.3) but does not fight back. Today you give it the two attacks your spec promised — a shockwave the player jumps and a charge the player sidesteps — both TELEGRAPHED, and both reading their numbers from a phase table so Phase 3 is a one-line change, not a rewrite.

Build Lab ~30 min

Attack 1 — the shockwave (you have the parts). It is a slow projectile fired along the ground: reuse 3.2's Projectile skeleton — a trigger collider moving by Translate — but flat and wide:

public class Shockwave : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private float speed = 3f;
    [SerializeField] private int damage = 1;
    [SerializeField] private float lifetime = 4f;

    private Vector2 direction;

    public void Initialize(Vector2 dir)
    {
        direction = dir.normalized;
    }

    private void Start()
    {
        Destroy(gameObject, lifetime);
    }

    private void Update()
    {
        transform.Translate(direction * speed * Time.deltaTime);
    }

    private void OnTriggerEnter2D(Collider2D other)
    {
        if (other.CompareTag("Player"))
        {
            if (StatManager.manager != null)
                StatManager.manager.ChangeHealth(-damage);
            Destroy(gameObject);
        }
    }
}

Why speed 3 (the turret's bullet is 10): a shockwave is a RHYTHM — slow enough to jump over ON PURPOSE. The wave is one tile tall; your jump clears two. That is the counterplay sentence from 8.1 made real.

Attack 2 — the charge. The boss's own body: telegraph 0.6s (it rears back — scale or color flash), then dashes horizontally at speed 8 for 0.8s, then recovers 1.5s (vulnerable — your reward window). BossManager grows a tiny attack scheduler in the starter's voice:

[SerializeField] private GameObject shockwavePrefab;
[SerializeField] private Transform shockwaveSpawn;
[SerializeField] private float attackInterval = 3f;
private float lastAttackTime;
private int currentPhase = 1;

private void Update()
{
    if (Time.time >= lastAttackTime + attackInterval && currentPhase > 1)
    {
        lastAttackTime = Time.time;
        FireShockwave();
        // charge is a coroutine or a state — studio choice
    }
}

private void FireShockwave()
{
    Vector2 dir = (playerTransform.position - transform.position).x > 0
        ? Vector2.right : Vector2.left;          // toward the player
    GameObject wave = Instantiate(shockwavePrefab,
        shockwaveSpawn.position, Quaternion.identity);
    wave.GetComponent<Shockwave>().Initialize(dir);
}

Read the ternary — one line picks a direction by comparing x positions. Same pursuit math as the chase (4.3), flattened to one axis.

The phase table. Attack numbers belong to PHASES, not to one set of serialized fields. Pattern: a small private table and one reader —

// phase: 1    2    3
// cooldown: 5s   3s   1.8s
// charge speed:  6    8    10

private void EnterPhase(int phase)
{
    currentPhase = phase;
    switch (phase)
    {
        case 2: attackInterval = 3f; chargeSpeed = 8f; break;
        case 3: attackInterval = 1.8f; chargeSpeed = 10f; break;
    }
}

Now Phase 3 is DIFFERENT because numbers changed, and the player SEES the difference without a tutorial. That is the whole trick of difficulty in fighting games.

Bug Hunt: The unreadable boss

  1. Set attackInterval to 0.5 in Phase 3. What happens to the jump rhythm — and what does "the player's counterplay must fit inside the attack interval" mean numerically for your wave speed?
  2. A shockwave spawns INSIDE the boss's collider and immediately touches the boss. Why does nothing happen (what tag does the boss carry vs the player)? Now spawn it inside the PLAYER by accident — what happens instead, and how does the 3.2 spawn-offset fix translate?
  3. The charge goes through walls (a physics-layer accident). What should stop a charge — and is a wall-stop a BUG or a FEATURE (the classic "stunned boss" gift)?
  4. Phase 3 activates while a shockwave is mid-flight. Does the OLD wave speed up retroactively? Why do instances keep their birth numbers — and when is that a problem (imagine a 20-second lifetime wave)?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Attack rhythm

  1. Play your own boss (spec says you must be able to beat it). Time the fight. If you cannot win, the boss is overtuned — a boss the designer cannot beat is not hard, it is broken.
  2. Add a third attack ONLY as a spec sentence first ("arena hazard spikes rise on a timer"). Do not code it — why does a written attack cost nothing and a coded one cost a day?
  3. Commit + push: "8.4a: shockwave + charge + phase table".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Build a telegraphed shockwave reusing the projectile pattern
  • Drive attack choice and pacing from a phase table
  • Explain counterplay arithmetic: wave height vs. jump height
  • Tune Phase 3 until you can beat your own boss
